title: Tenses Quiz 5
description: Choose will, going to, the present continuous or the present simple.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence shows a decision made at the moment of speaking?
options: I got a new phone yesterday evening.
I'm going to get a phone next week.
I have a meeting arranged for Friday.
The phone is ringing. I'll get it.
questions.explanation: A sudden decision uses will. Watch out: going to is for plans already made.

questions.question: Look at those dark clouds! It ___.
questions.explanation: We can see evidence, so be going to + base verb is used. Watch out: with it, the verb is is, not are.

questions.question: If it {{1}} (rain) tomorrow, we {{2}} (stay) at home.
questions.explanation: After if, use the present simple; the result uses will. Watch out: not if it will rain.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I call you when I will arrive.
I will call you when I arrive.
I will call you when I arrived.
I will call you when I will arrive.
questions.explanation: After when, a future meaning is shown by the present simple. Watch out: will never follows when in a time clause.

questions.question: At 8 pm tomorrow, I {{1}} (study).
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a future time uses will be + -ing.

questions.question: By next June, she {{1}} (finish) her degree.
questions.explanation: Finished before a future time: will have + past participle. Watch out: by + a time points to the future perfect.

questions.question: Match each form with its use.
right: an action in progress at a future time
an action finished before a future time
questions.explanation: Each form shows a different attitude to the future. Watch out: will have needs the past participle.

questions.question: 'I am meeting the doctor at four tomorrow' uses the present continuous for a future arrangement.
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for fixed arrangements. Watch out: there is a time and a person, so the plan is already arranged.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct for a timetable?
options: The train leaves at nine tomorrow.
The train will leaving at nine tomorrow.
The train has left at nine tomorrow.
The train is leave at nine tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Timetables use the present simple, even for the future. Watch out: will is followed by the base verb, never by -ing.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The future perfect is will have + past participle.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: I will phone you as soon as I will get home.
accepted: I will phone you as soon as I get home.
I will phone you as soon as I get home
I'll phone you as soon as I get home.
I'll phone you as soon as I get home
I’ll phone you as soon as I get home.
I’ll phone you as soon as I get home
questions.explanation: After as soon as, the present simple is used for the future. Watch out: will appears only in the main clause.
